title: Broncos officially put JK Dobbins on suspended list
summary: Broncos head coach Sean Payton announced on Tuesday that running back JK Dobbins was being suspended for conduct detrimental to the team and the move became official on Wednesday.
content: Broncos head coach Sean Payton announced on Tuesday that running back JK Dobbins was being suspended for conduct detrimental to the team and the move became official on Wednesday. The league's daily transaction report shows that Dobbins has officially been placed on the team's suspended list. He will forfeit a game check worth just over $222,222 as a result of the suspension keeping him out of Friday's game against the Steelers. The Broncos will also be without safety Taylor Rapp (quad) and defensive end Sai'Vion Jones (hamstring) after ruling them out on Wednesday's injury report. Running back Tyler Badie (thumb), wide receiver Pat Bryant (ankle), safety Brandon Jones (hamstring), tight end Caleb Lohner (foot), and safety JL Skinner (shoulder) were all full participants in practice.

title: PFT's Thanksgiving and Week 12 2026 NFL picks
summary: All games picked for one of the most compelling weeks of the season.
content: It was inevitable. After flirting a couple of times with landing under .500 in a given week of picks, it finally happened. For Week 11, I went 6-7. That's what I get for trying to pick upsets. In Week 11, it was Chalk City — and 12 of 13 home teams won. And so, from now on, I'm not getting cute. I'm sticking with my first impulse. I'm not overthinking it. The first number that pops into my head will be the pick. For the year, I'm at 102-60-1. The success rate is still 62.5 percent. Here's hoping I can find a way to push it a little higher with the 16 games to be played from Wednesday through Monday. Packers at Rams (Wednesday night) Sean McVay is 0-5 against Matt LaFleur. A loss on Wednesday night would put the preseason favorites in grave danger of missing the playoffs, especially in light of an upcoming schedule that includes games against the Chiefs, the 49ers, the Cowboys, the Seahawks (twice), and the Buccaneers. Rams 24, Packers 20. Bears at Lions (Thursday) It's the biggest early-window Thanksgiving game ever, with both teams at 8-2. Ben Johnson's Bears gave up 52 points during last year's visit to Ford Field. They'll be determined to achieve a different result this time, in what becomes a true litmus test for the new-look Bears. If they're truly contenders, this is a game they win. Bears 23, Lions 21. Eagles at Cowboys (Thursday) It won't be a cakewalk. For Philly, it's the closest they'll get this year to a game with a postseason vibe. But the Cowboys have a chance to make a run at the Giants — if Dallas can also hold off the Commanders. Cowboys 41, Eagles 24. Chiefs at Bills (Thursday) Josh Allen is 5-0 against Patrick Mahomes in the regular season, 0-4 against Mahomes in the postseason. The trend continues, thanks to conditions that are more conducive to Allen making the right throw at the right time. Bills 23, Chiefs 17. Broncos at Steelers (Friday) This one had the feel of a game the Steelers would find a way to win, until the benching of Aaron Rodgers threw everything into disarray. Broncos 20, Steelers 13. Saints at Bengals The Bengals need to get back on track, quickly, after Monday night's sluggish performance. A slump could open the door for the Browns to steal the division. Bengals 31, Saints 20. Ravens at Texans It feels like an elimination game in Houston, even if the winner will still be facing an uphill climb to the postseason. When in doubt, ride with the clearly better quarterback. Texans 27, Ravens 23. Giants at Colts This will be a far cry from the 1958 NFL Championship. The Giants are surging, and the Colts are slowly disintegrating. Giants 24, Colts 9. Titans at Jaguars As the saying goes, it's not the size of the dog in the fight but the size of the fight in the dog. Unfortunately, this fight is round two of Doberman vs. Chihuahua. Jaguars 35, Titans 20. Jets at Dolphins The Dolphins are running out of chances to get a second win (if they even want one). Dolphins 23, Jets 13. Falcons at Vikings Kirk Cousins gets the double whammy — his first home game in his second stint with the Vikings, and his first shot at revenge against the team that signed him and then drafted his replacement. Vikings 27, Falcons 13. Patriots at Chargers It's fitting that a game pitting two struggling teams coached by former Ohio State and Michigan players happens one day after a game between struggling Ohio State and Michigan teams. Patriots 16, Chargers 10. Commanders at Cardinals Monday night's upset of the Bengals means nothing if the Commanders bungle a winnable game at Arizona. Commanders 27, Cardinals 10. Seahawks at 49ers Having an extra week to prepare, coupled with the urgency of a 6-4 record, is just what the doctor ordered for the Seahawks. Seahawks 27, 49ers 23. Raiders at Browns The NFL will be happy it flexed this one into primetime. (For reasons other than getting Patriots-Chargers out of that window.) Browns 30, Raiders 27. Panthers at Buccaneers Tampa Bay is running out of chances to pull themselves back into contention. Buccaneers 27, Panthers 20.

title: Sam Darnold fully participates in Seahawks practice
summary: Seahawks quarterback Sam Darnold remains on track to return to the lineup for Sunday's game against the 49ers.
content: Seahawks quarterback Sam Darnold remains on track to return to the lineup for Sunday's game against the 49ers. Darnold was a full participant in practice after missing the last two games with quad and rib injuries. Head coach Mike Macdonald said before practice that Darnold's participation would be part of the final determination about his status for Sunday. "That's the plan, assuming practice goes well," Macdonald said, via the team's website. "Let's get through the practice, make sure everything feels good. He hasn't gone full speed yet since his injury, so this will be his first opportunity to go full speed." Linebacker DeMarcus Lawrence (shoulder), right tackle Abraham Lucas (ankle), quarterback Jalen Milroe (illness), left guard Quenton Nelson (knee), and defensive tackle Jarran Reed (toe) did not participate in practice. Guard Anthony Bradford (knee, illness), left tackle Charles Cross (ankle), linebacker Ernest Jones (knee), tight end Nick Kallerup (ankle), quarterback Drew Lock (right elbow), wide receiver Jaxon Smith-Njigba (ankle), and defensive tackle Leonard Williams (stinger) were limited participants.
